title: IEA TIMSS Japan: Cognitive Mastery, Affective Collapse, and Homework Fatigue in Mathematics and Science
source_name: IEA (International Association for the Evaluation of Educational Achievement) & NIER
description: Quadrennial international assessment evaluating 4th and 8th grade student attainment in mathematics and science, contrasting world-class cognitive scale scores with self-efficacy attrition, intrinsic motivation collapse, and homework load.
observation_unit: Cohort progression and cross-grade panel across TIMSS assessment cycles
sample_population_note: Nationally representative probability sample of Japanese 4th and 8th graders (approx. 10,000 students per cycle)
title_ja: 【IEA TIMSS】世界最高峰の認知得点と自己効力感崩壊（Grade 4 vs Grade 8）の乖離分析

research_angles.title: The Cognitive Elite vs Affective Burnout Paradox: Why Japanese Math Excellence Decouples from Student Self-Efficacy
research_questions: Why does secondary student self-efficacy plunge by more than 20 percentage points despite world-class test scores?
Does excessive homework duration explain the loss of intrinsic subject enjoyment in lower secondary school?
hypotheses: Cross-grade transition reveals an affective collapse where self-efficacy drops steeply while scale scores remain virtually identical.
Relational regression confirms that objective scale scores are entirely decoupled from student subjective enjoyment (R² < 0.05, VIF < 2.0).
research_angles.theoretical_framework: Expectancy-Value Theory (Eccles & Wigfield) and Self-Determination Theory (Ryan & Deci)
